reconciled_actions.rationale: The existing ATP-binding term gives the supported specificity of the nucleotide-binding function.

The exact PAO1 protein has an annotated ATP-binding site and conserved ABC ATPase architecture, consistent with the primary assignment of CbcV as the nucleotide-binding component. ATP binding is integral to energy coupling; these data do not report an isolated target binding affinity.

PMID21478341 measures PA14 choline growth across osmolarities: cbcV deletion is strongly detrimental at low osmolarity but not in the high-osmolarity growth comparison dominated by BetT3. Choline osmoprotection persists even after deletion of three transporters. These controls establish condition-dependent nutritional contributions, but neither isolate a PAO1 CbcV osmotic-response role nor demonstrate its absence; the electronic process claim remains unresolved.

CbcV supplies the ABC nucleotide-binding/ATPase component. PAO1 cbcXWV expression restores choline accumulation in transporter-deficient E. coli MKH13; empty vector is the negative control. CbcX supplies choline recognition, while the core executes translocation. PMID21478341 provides complementary PA14 growth/uptake evidence with PAO1 cbcXWV complementation, not a native PAO1 deletion assay.

The measured PAO1 CbcWV core transports carnitine when assembled with a compatible CaiX binding protein in E. coli MKH13. cbcV performs part of this transport activity; dependence on another complex subunit does not make the cargo-specific activity false for this participating subunit. CaiX selects the substrate, CbcW provides the membrane pathway, and CbcV supplies ATP coupling. Accept the target function and record contributes_to_molecular_function in core_functions, consistently with CaiX. The original machine-sourced enables qualifier is preserved. The assay establishes the assembled heterologous transporter activity, not autonomous subunit transport or native PAO1 uptake kinetics.

PMID23763788 Fig. 5 compares B728a BT binding-protein mutants carrying empty pN, pNCbcWV or pNCbcXWV. Core introduction restores COS-responsive QAC-uidA induction when CosX is present; cosX loss controls substrate recognition. PMID19919675 establishes that these core plasmids contain PAO1 cbcWV. This is controlled reporter evidence for cellular entry, not purified COS flux or native PAO1 COS physiology. Replace inorganic sulfate specificity with the supported quaternary ammonium transport class; COS is a sulfate ester, not free sulfate.

The direct PAO1-construct result is cellular glycine betaine accumulation in E. coli MKH13. PA14 growth/complementation links this import to nutritional use, but does not assign chemical breakdown to CbcV or CbcW. Retain the supported transport work by a lateral replacement to the existing glycine betaine-transport process; this is not a claim that transport is biologically unrelated to catabolism.

CbcW and CbcV provide membrane and ATPase components. Core-only expression in MKH13 lacks the uptake enabled by adding CaiX or CbcX, functionally establishing the substrate-binding-subunit-containing importer. Refine the general complex class to this supported importer architecture. PAINT places the ancestral claim at PANTHER:PTN002466744. The target is itself experimentally grounded among the descendant sources; its presence is not circular. No IRD/IKR loss was found on this lineage.
